Every catalog component as a custom element over the shared headless layer, in the product's accent.
`<pk-gate>` runs every screen the license calls for and renders your app inside. The React kit
draws the same DOM under the same stylesheet, so a state looks the same in both.

The package is private and the CDN module (`https://key.plrs.im/elements/<major>/pk.js`) is not
served yet. Until then the kit runs from a checkout of the repository.

<KitFacts kit="elements" />

## Install

Not on a feed yet. In the repository, build the package and import it:

```sh no-compile
mise exec node@22 -- pnpm --filter @polaris-key/elements build
```

Importing the module registers every element. It adds its stylesheet to the document itself,
through `adoptedStyleSheets`, never a `<style>` element. `PolarisKey.fonts(base)` says where Rubik
lives, or `PolarisKey.fonts(false)` when your page loads it.

## The one-line flow

Layer (a): wrap the app in `<pk-gate>`.

```html no-compile
<script type="module" src="./main.js"></script>

<pk-gate>
  <my-app></my-app>
</pk-gate>
```

The gate shows nothing while a cached session is checked. It renders the app once the license
holds, under the grace banner while offline grace runs. Until then it owns the window: Welcome,
the one sign-in form, Use a license key, Replace a device and the blocking states with their
fixes. Every control raises a `pk-action` event.

The gate takes its state from its `input` property today. A live adapter that drives it from the
SDK is not part of the kit yet.

## Piecemeal

Layer (b): each component is its own element (`pk-welcome`, `pk-activate`, `pk-sign-in`,
`pk-devices`, `pk-settings`, `pk-update-prompt` and the rest of the catalog), each with `::part`
hooks, named slots and `pk-*` events.

```html no-compile
<pk-sign-in presentation="sheet"></pk-sign-in>
```

Style a part with `::part(…)` and the `--pk-*` custom properties.

## Headless

Layer (c): `@polaris-key/elements/headless` re-exports ui-core's models, with no DOM, for a UI of
your own.

```ts no-compile
import { viewOf } from "@polaris-key/elements/headless";

const view = viewOf("Welcome", { gate: { status: "needs-activation" } });
console.log(view.state, view.copy);
```

## Theming

`PolarisKey.theme({…})` sets the theme for the page, `<pk-provider theme='{…}'>` for a subtree and
an element's `theme` property for one element. The fields are on
[Theming](/docs/build/ui/theming/). With no theme the kit draws the Polaris Key look in the
product's accent; `preset: "native"` restyles it to the host.

## Localisation

The eight launch locales load on demand from the generated copy tables. The locale is the theme's
`locale`, else the document's `lang`. `copy` overrides take a catalog key per locale; see
[Localization](/docs/build/ui/localization/).

## Sample

`examples/ui/elements/` gates a fixture product, Tidewater Studio, with `<pk-gate>` on the
fixtures, with no Worker. `?state=ok`, `grace`, `expired` or `revoked` pins the gate for one load.
The folder's README says how to run it. There is no `--live` switch yet.
